blocks.text: O ebony, O gold, O eagles of white ivory! Moreover, at Rome, as Pliny teaches, ebony held the third place in the esteem of tributes. Sixthly, although the Hebrews defer greatly to the Chaldee paraphrast, for whom הבנים hobnim are peacocks, they nevertheless acknowledge that some interpret it as ebony, and they waver between the two opinions. Hence Kimchi in his Commentaries: הובנים פירשו בו העץ הנקרא בערבי אבנוס, They interpret hobnim as the wood which is called ebony in Arabic. This is better than in his Lexicon, where it is יבנים jabnim, or jebenim. And Abarbanel: פירשו בו שהוא העץ הנקרא בערבי אוינוס שמביאין גם כן מארצות המזרח, They explain it as the wood which in Arabic is called evenus, which they also (like ivory) bring from the eastern lands. Mardochaeus and Aquinas: עצם חיה מה או מין עץ, The bone of some animal, or a kind of wood. Their repeated claim that it is the bone of an animal is a third opinion, which Kimchi explains in his Lexicon thus: הבנים הם חיות שעושין מלאכה מהעצם שלהן או מהקרנות כמו שעושין מעצם הפיל שהוא השן, Hobnim are animals from whose bones or horns certain works are made, as they are made from the bone of the elephant, which is ivory. But he reduces this third opinion to the first, which explains hobnim as peacocks, adding that it may be שיעשו מלאכה מעצם שלהם, that some work is made from their bones, namely as from ivory, with which הבנים hobnim is joined here. This is a monstrous opinion. For who has ever heard tell of peacock bones being carved or engraved, or used for any work in the manner of ivory? Thus the very fact that those who would have הבנים hobnim be peacocks slide into such absurd fictions shows how much more soundly those judge who understand ebony here; in that rendering there is nothing that does not fit exactly.
